newsitem.title: USA: Mass sets $271 mln variable rate sale for next wk.
newsitem.headline: Mass sets $271 mln variable rate sale for next wk.

text.p: Massachusetts plans to sell next week around $271 million of variable-rate refunding bonds after last week locking in a swap fixing its costs, Jeff Stearns, assistant deputy treasurer, said on Monday.

"We fixed the rate on the refunding and fixed the rate on the new money. In addition, we took bids on the swap variable-rate issue to be issued next week," said Stearns, explaining the variable-rate issue was part of last week's approximately $627 million fixed-rate bond sale.

Goldman Sachs and Ambac will be counterparties on the swap. Selling variable-rate bonds with a swap was expected to save the state around $5 million on an incremental basis. Massachusetts last did a swap in 1990, when it sold fiscal recovery bonds.

While the state opted to advance to last week the big bond sale, which included an approximately $377 million refunding, in order to take advantage of a recent drop in interest rates, the state official added that bond prices would have to rally further to make another refunding economic.
"There would have to be a nice run-up," said Stearns, explaining the state needs to capture a four-percent savings when measured on a present value basis.
